problem:
Given that $L{{e}^{at}}=\frac{1}{s-a}$ for $s>a$, find the Laplace transform of
$g(t)={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{4τ}\,\text{d}τ$
for $s>4.$
worked_solution:
We know that if $L{f(t)}=F(s)$, then

$$
L{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

In our case, $f(t)={e}^{4t}.$ Thus, for $s>4,$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & =L{f(t)} \\  & =L{{e}^{4t}} \\  & =\frac{1}{s-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying the integral identity above, we have that for $s>4,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{g(t)} & =L{{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{4τ}\,\text{d}τ} \\  & =\frac{F(s)}{s} \\  & =\frac{1}{s(s-4)}.\end{aligned}
$$
